analysis: A pinned in-process AVC checkpoint owns codec-aware state through FFmpeg SPS/PPS/reference retention, DPB pointer rebasing and POC/MMCO/SEI copying, not raw context memcpy. At the fully drained no-B picture30 boundary, three restored30-picture suffixes remain host-exact after each prior live decoder reaches EOF. All source/runtime/owner/version/cut guards and dropped-handle rejection pass. Seven paired prepared-runtime jobs include checkpoint construction and3scrubs: median0.8343x replay cost, paired bootstrap95 ratio[0.7777,0.9844]. Cold startup is noisier (median0.9042x, range0.2065–1.3971), so pursue bounded already-loaded scrubbing only. This is a versioned in-process owned handle, not a portable serialized checkpoint or cross-runtime state import. Public decoder parameters initialize a fresh codec context, then the codec-specific maintained state copier retains/rebases its logical fields. No browser decoder state export. Profile is AVC progressive8bit420, noB, fully consumed output; no arbitrary threading, queued outputs, resolution transitions, durable storage or physical-memory saving claim. Source-context pointers are never copied wholesale.
